identity.name: Jinghai Circuit
alt_names: Viet principality of the Khúc clan

land.text: Annan, retaken by Gao Pian in autumn 866 and renamed Jinghai Jun
'Ngo Quyen proclaimed himself king and chose the town of Co Loa as the capital' in spring 939

successors.note: The ngo-dynasty dossier names southern-han as its predecessor; the Southern Han only held the circuit from October 930 to 931, so this circuit is the nearer predecessor.

capitals.name: Songping (Đại La, Hanoi)
capitals.note: Gao Pian 'recaptured Songping, the capital of Annan'; in 880 the army 'mutinied, taking the city of Đại La'; Duong Dinh Nghe besieged the Southern Han garrison at Đại La in 931 (Dương Đình Nghệ page).

rulers.name: Gao Pian
rulers.title: Jinghai jiedushi
rulers.note: Served as jiedushi 866-868; his grandson Kao Xun took charge after 868.

rulers.name: Tang governors
rulers.title: short-term appointed governors
rulers.note: 'From 880 to 905, the Tang appointed a series of short-term governors' who held no real power.

rulers.name: Khúc Thừa Dụ
rulers.title: jiedushi
rulers.note: Tang recognition 'in the first month of 906'; died in the seventh month of 907.

rulers.name: Khúc Hạo
rulers.title: jiedushi
rulers.note: Died in 919 (the Dương Đình Nghệ page).

rulers.name: Khúc Thừa Mỹ
rulers.title: jiedushi
rulers.note: Captured by the Southern Han in autumn 923 on the Dương Đình Nghệ page; 930 in Chinese sources and on the Bạch Đằng page.

rulers.name: Dương Đình Nghệ
rulers.title: jiedushi
rulers.note: Took Đại La in 931; murdered in March 937.

rulers.name: Kiều Công Tiễn
rulers.title: usurper
rulers.note: Seized power in March 937; executed by Ngô Quyền before the Southern Han army arrived.

rulers.name: Ngô Quyền
rulers.title: jiedushi, then king from spring 939
rulers.note: Defeated the Southern Han fleet at the Bạch Đằng in late 938.

correction.text: the Jinghai Circuit: the Annan of the Tang, northern Vietnam from the Red River delta to Thanh Hoa, Nghe An and Ha Tinh, seat at Songping (Dai La, Hanoi)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Neither the Annan page nor the Khúc, Dương Đình Nghệ or Bạch Đằng pages define the circuit's territory (the last: 'does not define the circuit's exact territory'); the shape is the Annan protectorate's, with Ái Châu (Thanh Hóa) named as part of the circuit's south. Cliopatria's Ngô row has northern Vietnam only from 947 (62,155 km2), so the shape stands unverified against an infobox area.

region.text: the Jinghai Circuit: the Annan of the Tang, northern Vietnam from the Red River delta to Thanh Hoa, Nghe An and Ha Tinh, seat at Songping (Dai La, Hanoi)

ledger.note: 866: Gao Pian founds the Jinghai Circuit. He 'recaptured Songping, the capital of Annan' and 'renamed the region of Annan to Jinghai Jun'; he served as Jinghai jiedushi 866-868. The Tang-Nanzhao page gives no month for the renaming.

880: the garrison mutinies. 'In 880, the army in Annan mutinied, taking the city of Đại La', ending de facto Chinese control of northern Vietnam; the Tang appoint short-term governors until 905 (Khúc Thừa Dụ page).

906: the Khúc clan is recognised. Khúc Thừa Dụ's tenure begins in 905 and 'the Tang emperor had to accept the autonomy of that region' by giving him the jiedushi post 'in the first month of 906' (the page marks this as needing a citation); he dies in the seventh month of 907 and his son Khúc Hạo 'continued to consolidate the autonomy of Tĩnh Hải quân'.

930: the Southern Han invade. In October 930 they 'launched an attack on the Jinghai circuit, which at the time was a Viet principality controlled by the Khúc clan' (the Dương Đình Nghệ page dates the capture of Khúc Thừa Mỹ to autumn 923). Mirror of southern-han's 930 occupation.

931: Dương Đình Nghệ drives them out. He 'raised a 3,000-men army of retainers and drove the Southern Han back to the borders of the Jinghai Circuit', besieged and took Đại La and proclaimed himself jiedushi (Dương Đình Nghệ page).

937: Dương Đình Nghệ is murdered. In March 937 Kiều Công Tiễn 'murders him and seizes power'; Ngô Quyền, his son-in-law, defeats and executes Kiều, who had appealed to the Southern Han emperor Liu Yan.

region.text: the Jinghai Circuit: the Annan of the Tang, northern Vietnam from the Red River delta to Thanh Hoa, Nghe An and Ha Tinh, seat at Songping (Dai La, Hanoi)

ledger.note: 939: Ngô Quyền becomes king. In late 938 he beats Liu Hongcao's Southern Han fleet at the Bạch Đằng ('half of the Han army died ... including Liu Hongcao'); in spring 939 he 'proclaimed himself king and chose the town of Co Loa as the capital', ending the circuit.

wars.name: Southern Han attack on the Jinghai Circuit

zones.text: Đại La and the Hanoi plain

wars.outcome: The Southern Han took the circuit in October 930; Dương Đình Nghệ retook Đại La and drove them to the border in 931.

wars.name: Battle of Bạch Đằng (938)
wars.outcome: Ngô Quyền's fleet destroyed the Southern Han fleet led by Liu Hongcao at the mouth of the Bạch Đằng River in late 938; Liu Yan retreated to Guangzhou and Ngô Quyền proclaimed himself king in spring 939.

certainty.note: No page defines the circuit's territory; the Chinese frontier on the north and the Cham frontier on the south are approximate.

sources.title: Protectorate General to Pacify the South
sources.note: 866 renaming, Gao Pian 866-868, the 880 mutiny at Đại La.

sources.title: Dương Đình Nghệ
sources.note: Khúc Hạo 919, the 923/930 capture of Khúc Thừa Mỹ, Dương Đình Nghệ 931, his murder in March 937, Ngô Quyền.

sources.title: Tang-Nanzhao conflicts in Annan
sources.note: Gao Pian's 866 retaking; no month for the renaming.

notes: New state (Cliopatria has no row; its Ngo Dynasty row begins 947 and the ngo-dynasty dossier names southern-han as predecessor, which should be this circuit). The English Wikipedia has no page titled 'Jinghai Circuit' that was opened; wikipedia is null. Open points: (1) the circuit's territory is not defined on any page, so the Annan shape is carried; (2) the capture of Khúc Thừa Mỹ is autumn 923 on the Dương Đình Nghệ page and 930 on the Bạch Đằng page, and the dossier uses 930 for the occupation; (3) the Tang dossier's 866 gain of Annan from nanzhao stays valid up to 880; from 880 the circuit is de facto autonomous, which no Tang event records; (4) southern-han's occupation events name the counterpart 'Jinghai circuit' (no slug), which should become jinghai-circuit; (5) Gao Pian left in 868 on the Annan page but the Tang-Nanzhao page does not mention 868.
